entities.summary:
Marie de Coucy (marie-de-coucy) was a prominent figure in the medieval world, serving as Queen of Alba by marriage to King Alexander II. Born into a noble family, she rose to prominence during the reign of her son, Alexander III, who ruled from 1249 to 1286. Marie de Coucy played a key role in the royal council, advising her son on matters of state and diplomacy. Her influence extended to the entire kingdom, as she worked to maintain peace and stability during a tumultuous period in European history.

As queen, Marie de Coucy oversaw the administration of the kingdom, managing its finances and overseeing the construction of infrastructure projects. She also played a crucial role in the development of the kingdom's economy, encouraging trade and commerce. Her efforts helped to establish Alba as a major power in the region, fostering alliances with neighboring kingdoms and securing valuable trade agreements.

Despite her many accomplishments, Marie de Coucy's legacy is often overshadowed by that of her son and husband. However, her contributions to the kingdom's history cannot be overstated, and her influence continues to be felt in the modern era. She remains an important figure in the study of medieval European history, offering valuable insights into the lives of women in power during this period.

Marie de Coucy's life and reign serve as a reminder of the enduring impact of women in shaping the course of history. Her remarkable story is a testament to the power and resilience of women in the face of adversity, inspiring future generations to pursue careers in politics, diplomacy, and leadership.
